World's First Aero-Electric Travel Trailer Is a Futuristic Home for 4 That Expands at Camp
26 photos
Photo: Lightship
Some three years ago, U.S.-based startup Lightship broke on the RV scene with a concept for a travel trailer – of the future! – that went viral almost immediately. Initially called the Lightship L1, that futuristic RV has grown into the Lightship AE.1 and now, as a 2027 model year, is shipping to first customers nationwide.
Lightship AE.1 is dubbed the world's first aero-electric travel trailer, but as neat as that might sound, it's not even the most impressive thing about it. That would be the sum of all its features: its self-sufficiency, its low profile in travel mode and yet the ability to offer true creature comforts, its sustainability, and its ultra-smart characteristics.
This travel trailer is unlike any other on the market right now, and that's not just a way of saying. It was designed to be different, built to be different, and the result is – obviously – different.
The AE.1 debuted in prototype form at the 2025 CES in Las Vegas, almost two years after its introduction as a concept at SXSW. At the time, limited production for the founders' edition, which Lightship called the AE.1 Cosmos Edition, was scheduled to kick off by the summer of that year, with deliveries for those 50 first units to follow.
Photo: Lightship Lightship is now saying that production is on track, so that probably means that plans announced for the other three trims, Atmos, Panos, and Terros, will probably proceed as scheduled as well. Before that happens, though, Lightship is offering a better look at the 2027 AE.1 through the video tour below, taking place at their California facility.
Here's Many of Beer Run Bus touring the 2027 version of the viral travel trailer and then getting a tour of the facility. It's the perfect chance to see what modifications Lightship has implemented as well as to see how the production version of the 2025 prototype is shaping up. This video tour also offers a bunch of new specs that weren't made public with the debut of that prototype.
Designed & built different As already noted, the Lightship AE.1 is different in every aspect you can think of. Built on a steel chassis with aluminum frame and fiberglass body, it comes with an interior packed with sustainable and extra-durable materials, from the woven vinyl flooring to the composite underfloor and composite counters.
Photo: Lightship Cabinetry is all aluminum, with lattice-style doors and full aluminum construction, both for the drawers and cabinets. The upholstery is recycled plastic and wool, so it's durable, dirt-resistant, and nice to the touch, offering a homey vibe to offset the rather austere, almost sterile interior walls.
The layout is different from a traditional travel trailer , too, because Lightship opts to have a canopy roof that lifts and lowers on actuators for an easier towing experience. That means that you can't have actual rooms inside, and the only door and wall you'll find onboard are to the rear, full-width bathroom.
Dimensions haven't changed. The AE.1 is a 26.7 feet (8.1 meters) long, 8.5 feet (2.5 meters) wide, and 7 feet (2.1 meters) high in travel mode, expanding to 10 feet (3 meters) in total height at camp to offer 7.5 feet (2.2 meters) of interior headroom.
Photo: Lightship Gross weight is 8,300 lbs (3,765 kg) but the AE.1 is meant to offer a comparable easier towing experience thanks to the TrekDrive system on the tandem axle, consisting of a 400V motor moving the wheels in conjunction with the array of sensors in the vicinity of the towbar. Lightship AE.1 is meant to reduce the impact on the range of the towing vehicle, whether it's an electric or a gas-fueled one.
Another way in which towing impact is reduced is through enhanced aerodynamics , which is where the collapsible canopy comes in. It's not just an aesthetic choice or a weird flex, helping reduce drag by effectively scaling down the footprint of the trailer behind the towing vehicle.
Control of the canopy is either manual, with a physical button available on the box at the front, or fully automated, through the companion Atlas app you can use on the provided tablet/touchscreen panel or your phone. For extra safety, Lightship includes a thorough checklist of stuff you should be mindful of before closing down the canopy.
Photo: Lightship Large, frameless and slightly tinted windows with integrated blinds and flyscreens offer 270-degree panoramic views inside. The interior remains usable even with the canopy down, though you won't be enjoying the views in that case. You won't have full functionality inside, but you can still sit down for a quick meal, get some work done, have a nap, or use the bathroom.
Self-sufficiency & comfort The Lightship AE.1 comes with as much as 77kWh of lithium batteries built into the steel underbody chassis and a roof lined with 1,800W of solar panels. That's more than enough to run house functions without restrictions, to charge the towing vehicle, or even use the massive battery bank as backup for the home in case of an emergency.
Photo: Lightship Also on the topic of autonomy, the AE.1 carries 50 gallons (189 liters) of freshwater, 25 gallons (95 liters) of gray, and 30 gallons (113.5 liters) of black water.
Inside, you have a Switchback Lounge at the front, which is a lounge arrangement with two levels and a mattress that flips out into a queen bed. That's one of the two available sleeping spaces, not including the optional Summit Sleeper, which is a double drop down bed that's not included in the demo unit.
The other sleeping space is the dinette, which converts by dropping the table at the press of another button. During the day, it's spacious and comfortable to sit up to six people, but it will only accommodate two of them at night.
Photo: Lightship The kitchen starts to left side of the extra-wide entry way, so you have plenty of worktop space and a decent amount of storage options. A large, stainless steel sink is available as you advance to the rear of the trailer, across from the main kitchen block, which is equipped with a two-burner induction cooktop, a water-efficient dishwasher, a convection microwave oven, and a marine-grade fridge with freezer.
Again, storage is limited to the lower part of the trailer, but Lightship compensates for that with the modular CargoCraft modular storage system consisting of open cubbies you attach on rail tracks over the windows – and subsequently remove when you pack up camp to head back home.
The full-width bathroom is hidden behind opaque plastic walls and comes with a plumbed porcelain toilet, a small sink with storage below and overhead, and a flush-floor shower with a curtain. Being built out of the same easy-to-dry and easy-to-clean composites, not having a step-up or step-in shower allows it to be extra spacious and comfortable.
Photo: Lightship The Lightship AE.1 also comes with electric auto-leveling, four corner stabilizers, a backup camera, three exterior color choices, a large pass-through storage compartment at the front, a Seaflo water pump, and a 20,000-BTU AC unit with a heat pump inside the front box that services the entire trailer.
Prices start at around $157,000 for the most basic version and go as high as $250,000 for the Cosmos variant shown below.
